questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why marriages end and how different countries respond to divorce
How to plan a wedding
Famous pop songs about love
Why people in China marry young
questions.why: They hear how divorce is talked about in different countries and why couples separate.

questions.q: What has happened to divorce rates since the 1990s?
options: They have risen everywhere, especially in Europe and America
They have stayed the same
They have slowed in the West but are rising elsewhere
They have fallen everywhere
questions.why: Georgie says Western divorce rates have slowed, while in other parts of the world they're rising.

questions.q: What are two common reasons for couples growing apart, according to Phil?
options: Having too many children and moving house
Money problems and working too much
Living abroad, far from family, and speaking different languages at home
Marrying very young and having different backgrounds or interests
questions.why: He says getting married very young and differences in background or interests are two common causes.

questions.q: What do we learn about Professor Marina Adshade's marriage?
options: She married later in life, after she had finished her university degree
She married young, without education, to an older, educated man
She married someone younger than her
She and her husband studied together
questions.why: She says she married really young with no education, to someone older with a lot of education.

questions.q: What change caused problems in Marina's marriage?
options: Her husband lost his job and they had to move to a different city for work
She decided to go back to school and stop being a stay-at-home mother
They moved to a new country
They decided not to have children
questions.why: In her late 20s she went back to school and no longer wanted to be a stay-at-home mother.

questions.q: Why do many people stay in marriages that no longer work?
options: Because the law doesn't allow divorce
Because they are too busy
Because their friends tell them to stay
For economic or emotional reasons
questions.why: Georgie says many people stay trapped due to economic or emotional reasons.

questions.q: What did the Chinese government introduce in 2021?
options: A 30-day waiting period for couples who want to separate
A ban on divorce
Free relationship counselling for all married couples in the country
A tax on weddings
questions.why: Georgie says China introduced a 30-day cooling-off period for couples wanting to separate.

questions.q: What does divorce counsellor Joanna Gosling think would help more than a cooling-off period?
options: Longer waiting periods
Stricter divorce laws
Government programmes to help couples communicate
Making weddings more expensive so that fewer people marry young
questions.why: She suggests states invest in communication programmes, because that's why relationships fall apart.
